adrenaline.description: Excitement and visceral exhilaration during viewing.

tension.description: Suspense, dread, or anticipation of an uncertain outcome.

fear.description: Fright or horror experienced, independently of horror genre membership.

perceived_threat.description: Sense that characters face harm, including harm never shown.

romantic_feeling.description: Romantic affection or longing evoked in the viewer.

sensuality.description: Erotic atmosphere or sexual tension, independently of explicit sexual depiction.

warmth.description: Affectionate, kind, or emotionally welcoming tone.

wholesomeness.description: Reassurance through care, kindness, and emotional safety.

wonder.description: Awe, amazement, or fascination with discovery.

pathos.description: Acute pity, sorrow, or tragic emotional impact.

uncanniness.description: Unease from the strangely familiar or almost natural.

catharsis.description: Emotional release after accumulated tension or feeling.

nostalgia.description: Longing for a remembered or imagined past evoked by the work; not release age.

hopefulness.description: Optimistic outlook or belief in positive possibilities.

emotional_intensity.description: Overall strength of emotional engagement, regardless of positive or negative tone.

stress.description: Sustained pressure, discomfort, or anxiety experienced during viewing.

uplift.description: Encouragement, joy, or improved spirits evoked.

thought_provocation.description: Invitation to reflect on ideas, ethics, or interpretations beyond the immediate plot.

playfulness.description: Light, mischievous, or freely inventive tone.

sentimentality.description: Overt appeal to tender feelings and emotional attachment.

emotional_restraint.description: Understated expression and withholding of overt emotional display.

bittersweetness.description: Positive and painful feelings intertwined rather than merely appearing separately.

absurdity.description: Experience of incongruity, illogic, or strangeness, whether humorous or unsettling.

escapism.description: Immersion away from everyday concerns; not limited to fantasy settings.

wish_fulfillment.description: Invitation to imagine desired powers, relationships, status, or ways of life.

tranquility.description: Calm, restful or meditative feeling evoked; not merely absence of tension.

indignation.description: Moral outrage or righteous anger evoked in the viewer; distinct from anger depicted by characters.

disgust.description: Revulsion evoked, independently of comic gross-out, frightening threat or grotesque visual style.

overall.description: Overall amount and strength of comedy, independently of individual humor styles.

situational.description: Humor from circumstances, misunderstandings, and complications; no episodic-format requirement.

wit_wordplay.description: Humor from verbal cleverness, puns, or linguistic ambiguity.

physical.description: Humor from bodily action, slapstick, or visual physical mishaps.

cringe.description: Humor from embarrassment or uncomfortable social situations.

absurdist.description: Humor from nonsense, illogic, or bizarre juxtapositions.

satire.description: Humorous critique of institutions, behavior, or social conventions.

parody.description: Humorous imitation of a recognizable work, genre, or style.

dark.description: Humor about death, suffering, taboo, or tragedy.

running_gags.description: Recurring jokes whose repetition or variation creates humor.

meta.description: Humor about storytelling, production, audiences, or the work itself.

deadpan.description: Humor delivered with apparent seriousness or minimal emotional reaction.

gross_out.description: Humor relying on bodily fluids, disgust, or vulgar physical material.

crime.description: Criminal acts and their consequences as subject matter.

mystery.description: Uncovering an important unknown as a central concern.

war.description: Armed conflict and its human or societal consequences.

politics.description: Governance, political institutions, and struggles for political power.

radicalization.description: A process of adopting increasingly extreme ideological commitments or endorsing extremist action. Distinct from existing political beliefs, ordinary persuasion, rebellion, group secrecy, and coercive group control; those alone do not establish radicalization.

family.description: Family bonds, conflict, obligations, and belonging.

psychology.description: Mental processes, internal conflict, or perception as subject matter.

entertainment_industry.description: The business and practice of entertainment and celebrity.

social_critique.description: Examination or criticism of social arrangements and norms.

class.description: Social class, economic inequality, and mobility.

capitalism.description: Economic systems organized around capital, profit, and ownership.

consumerism.description: Exploration or critique of acquiring goods, consumption, brands, or possessions as a source of identity, status, or fulfillment. Distinct from capitalism as an economic system; buying or using a product alone is insufficient.

technological_change.description: Exploration of societal or personal effects of technological development, adoption, or displacement, including effects on work, relationships, institutions, and identity. Gadget presence, advanced technology, or science alone is insufficient.

human_nature.description: Explicit thematic exploration of what humans are like: capacities, impulses, morality, cooperation, cruelty, or tensions between nature and social conditioning. Ordinary human characters, emotion, or drama alone is insufficient; not a synonym for personal identity, consciousness, or existential meaning.

faith_and_spirituality.description: Religious belief, spiritual practice, or metaphysical meaning.

business.description: Commercial organizations, enterprise, and work decisions.

finance.description: Money management, financial systems, investing, or debt.

environment.description: Relationships between human activity and ecosystems.

science.description: Scientific inquiry and its ideas, practice, or consequences.

popular_culture.description: Popular media, celebrity, fandom, or shared cultural trends.

survival.description: Meeting essential needs or overcoming threats to continued life.

adventure.description: Exploration, risk, and discovery outside ordinary life.

hacking.description: Intrusion into or manipulation of computer systems.

artificial_intelligence.description: Artificial agents and their interaction with the world.

consciousness.description: The nature of subjective experience and personhood.

identity.description: Formation, discovery, concealment, or change of personal identity.

existential_meaning.description: Purpose, freedom, mortality, and the meaning of existence.

trauma.description: Lasting effects of overwhelming or harmful experiences.

recovery.description: Processes of rebuilding after trauma, illness, or crisis.

mental_health.description: Mental health conditions, care, and lived experience.

addiction.description: Dependency and its effects on people and relationships.

addiction_recovery.description: Attempts to overcome dependency and maintain recovery.

trust_and_betrayal.description: Reliance on others, deception, and broken trust.

coming_of_age.description: Development toward adult identity, agency, or responsibility.

coming_out.description: Disclosure or recognition of LGBTQ identity in a social context.

sexuality.description: Sexual identity, desire, and their social meaning.

gender_identity.description: Gender identity and its personal or social implications. Distinct from social expectations about gender roles and from sexism; do not infer identity from conformity to or rejection of a role.

gender_roles.description: Exploration of social expectations, norms, or performances of masculinity, femininity, and gendered roles. Distinct from a person's gender identity and from sexism as discrimination; either may coexist without implying the other.

immigration.description: Migration across borders and the experience of settlement.

displacement.description: Loss of home or community through conflict, coercion, or other forces.

gentrification.description: Neighborhood change associated with investment and displacement.

surveillance.description: Monitoring, privacy, and control through observation.

disease_and_pandemics.description: Population-level disease transmission, epidemics, pandemics or public-health response matter as subjects. Personal diagnosis, dying and care are assessed separately as illness_and_dying.

climate_change.description: Climate processes, human causes, or consequences.

inherited_wealth.description: Inheritance, dynastic wealth, and intergenerational economic advantage.

social_media.description: Online social platforms and their effects on life.

public_shaming.description: Public condemnation, reputational punishment, or social exclusion.

forgiveness.description: Letting go of blame or reconciling after harm.

loyalty.description: Commitment to people, groups, or principles under pressure.

belonging.description: Acceptance, community, and finding a place among others.

loneliness.description: Isolation and unmet desire for connection.

ambition.description: Pursuit of achievement, status, or recognition.

labor.description: Working conditions, worker identity, organizing, and exploitation.

colonialism.description: Colonial domination, resistance, and its legacies.

racism.description: Racial discrimination and its personal or structural consequences.

sexism.description: Discrimination or domination based on sex or gender.

caregiving.description: Responsibility for another person's everyday support and wellbeing.

parenthood.description: Becoming or being a parent and its consequences.

aging.description: Later life, changing capacities, and social experiences of aging.

midlife.description: Reassessment and transitions in middle adulthood.

retirement.description: Leaving paid work and adjusting to life afterward.

early_adulthood.description: Independence, work, and relationships in early adult life.

artistic_creation.description: Making art and the motivations or struggles involved.

persuasion_and_propaganda.description: Shaping public or interpersonal belief through persuasion, spin, PR, advertising, propaganda or disinformation is a subject of the work; do not label the work itself propaganda from this score.

illness_and_dying.description: Personal illness, diagnosis, living with illness, dying or end-of-life care is a subject; distinct from population-level epidemics.

corruption.description: Abuse of entrusted public, organizational or professional power for private gain is a subject; not all crime or ambition is corruption.

investigation.description: Characters gather evidence to explain an event or identify responsibility.

pursuit.description: An extended chase or hunt organizes the story.

rescue.description: Saving someone from captivity or danger organizes the story.

escape.description: Getting out of confinement or an unsafe situation organizes the story.

quest.description: A journey toward a defined objective organizes the story.

competition.description: A contest with rivals and an outcome organizes the story.

relationship_development.description: Changes in a relationship organize the story.

everyday_life.description: Ordinary routines and small events organize the story.

survival.description: Remaining alive under threatening conditions organizes the story.

heist.description: Planning, carrying out, or dealing with a theft organizes the story.

espionage.description: Secret intelligence gathering or covert state operations organize the story.

military_operation.description: An organized military mission structures the story.

legal_case.description: Court proceedings, formal adjudication or preparation for a legal case organize the story. Legislative debate or a political committee hearing alone belongs to political_struggle.

political_struggle.description: Pursuit or exercise of political power structures the story.

underdog_rise.description: An initially disadvantaged character gains standing or succeeds against stronger opposition.

revenge.description: Retaliation for a perceived wrong drives an arc.

fall_from_grace.description: A character loses status, reputation, or moral standing.

redemption.description: A character attempts to make amends or change after wrongdoing.

romantic_development.description: Formation or deepening of a romantic relationship matters to the story.

established_couple.description: An ongoing romantic partnership matters to the story; former partners or separated co-parents alone belong to breakup_or_divorce or parent_child.

breakup_or_divorce.description: Ending a partnership matters to the story.

partner_bereavement.description: Loss of a romantic partner matters to the story.

love_triangle.description: Competing romantic attachments among three people matter to the story.

forbidden_romance.description: A romantic relationship faces a consequential social or institutional prohibition.

friendship.description: Non-romantic bonds of friendship matter to the story.

mentor_mentee.description: Guidance and learning between mentor and mentee matter to the story.

rivalry.description: Competition or mutual opposition between characters matters to the story.

forced_proximity.description: Circumstances oblige characters to remain close or share space.

adversaries_cooperate.description: Characters with genuinely opposing goals cooperate in a consequential shared undertaking; friendly peers in different industries are not automatically adversaries.

found_family.description: Chosen bonds serve a family-like role in the story.

family_conflict.description: Sustained conflict or harmful dysfunction within a family matters to the story.

intergenerational.description: Relationships across generations matter to the story.

generational_trauma.description: Trauma transmitted or repeated across generations matters to the story.

parent_child.description: The relationship between parent and child matters to the story.

siblings.description: Sibling relationships matter to the story.

caregiver_dependent.description: Care and dependence between characters matter to the story.

human_animal_companionship.description: An emotional bond between a person and animal matters to the story.

coercive_relationship.description: Manipulation, coercion, or control within an interpersonal relationship matters to the story. Systematic control of members by a group is assessed separately as coercive_group_control; neither automatically implies the other.

coercive_group_control.description: A group or leader systematically controls members through intimidation, isolation, dependency, punishment, or suppression of autonomy. Distinct from interpersonal coercion, voluntary discipline, secrecy, and radicalization; any of these may coexist but does not imply group control.

ensemble.description: Several focal characters share narrative attention and agency.

antihero.description: A focal character departs substantially from conventional heroic ethics or behavior.

morally_ambiguous_cast.description: Moral ambiguity among multiple major characters matters to the work.

transformation_arc.description: Substantial change in a focal character's beliefs, identity, or behavior.

intellectual_problem_solver.description: A focal character's reasoning or specialized intellectual ability drives events.

detective_lead.description: A focal character acts as an investigator or detective.

workplace_team.description: A team formed through work is a central social unit.

family_business.description: A family-run business is a central social unit.

unaccompanied_children.description: Children without their usual caregivers form a central social situation.

teen_peer_group.description: Teenage friendships and peer-group dynamics form a central social situation.

clandestine_groups.description: A secret society or organized group whose membership, meetings, activities, or aims are deliberately concealed. Secrecy is the defining feature, not coercion or extremist ideology; a secret held by one person, an ordinary private friendship, or crime alone is insufficient.

advanced_technology.description: Technology substantially beyond the work's contemporary baseline shapes its world.

magic.description: Supernatural abilities or forces understood as magic shape the world.

simulation.description: An artificial simulation is an important layer of depicted reality. A physically staged real environment or social deception alone is not a simulation.

virtual_reality.description: Characters experience an interactive digitally mediated environment. A physical set, surveillance broadcast or deception alone is not virtual reality.

parallel_worlds.description: Coexisting alternative realities matter to the world.

time_travel.description: Movement across time outside ordinary chronological passage matters to the world.

time_loop.description: Repetition of a period of time matters to the world or narrative.

dystopian_society.description: Oppressive or deeply dysfunctional social arrangements define the world.

post_apocalyptic.description: Life after a civilization-scale catastrophe defines the world.

spacefaring.description: Travel or life beyond Earth is consequential to the world.

robots.description: Embodied artificial machines functioning as agents matter to the world; not synonymous with AI.

myth_and_folklore.description: Recognizable mythological or folkloric traditions shape the world.

scientific_rigor.description: Attention to scientific constraints and explanatory consistency; not an inverse of speculative freedom.

speculative_freedom.description: Freedom to use speculative premises without scientific elaboration.

worldbuilding_depth.description: Detail and interconnection in the world's institutions, history, and rules.

magic_rule_detail.description: Elaboration of rules and constraints governing magic.

everyday_realism.description: Attention to plausible ordinary behavior and material conditions, independently of era.

magical_realism.description: Impossible or supernatural events are treated as ordinary within an otherwise everyday world; distinct from an explicitly elaborated magic system.

plot_velocity.description: Rate at which consequential plot events occur.

gradual_development.description: Deliberate accumulation of character, relationships, or tension over time; can coexist with rapid action.

intrigue.description: Strength of curiosity about what happens or what is concealed.

plot_complexity.description: Interdependence of events, causes, and plot threads.

interpretive_ambiguity.description: Extent to which meaning or events support multiple interpretations.

twist_frequency.description: Recurrence of major reversals or revelations over the work.

twist_impact.description: Extent to which revelations alter understanding or expectations.

multiple_timelines.description: Use of distinct temporal strands; not necessarily time travel.

multiple_viewpoints.description: Distribution of storytelling across distinct character perspectives.

unreliable_narration.description: Uncertainty created by an unreliable narrator or viewpoint.

unreliable_reality.description: Uncertainty about which presented events or reality layers are real.

self_reference.description: Attention to the work's own storytelling or construction.

fourth_wall_breaking.description: Explicit acknowledgment of the audience or of the work as a presented fiction, including direct address. Voiceover alone is not sufficient.

voiceover.description: Use of spoken narration over images outside ordinary scene dialogue.

dream_sequences.description: Use of dreams or hallucinations as presented sequences.

observational_mode.description: Attention to behavior and environments without strong explanatory or plot intervention.

slice_of_life.description: Emphasis on ordinary experience rather than extraordinary plot escalation.

exposition_load.description: Amount of explanatory information the viewer must absorb.

information_withholding.description: Deliberate delay in supplying information needed to understand events.

formal_challenge.description: Departure from familiar formal conventions that demands adaptation.

didacticism.description: How explicitly the work states, teaches or argues a message; independent of intellectual stimulation or whether the viewer agrees.

confined_setting.description: Concentration of the work within a single location or tightly bounded connected spaces; distinct from small cast, low budget or confinement as a plot event.

personal.description: Consequences for an individual's life, identity, or goals.

relationship.description: Consequences for a central relationship or small social unit.

community.description: Consequences for a locality or community.

societal.description: Consequences for institutions, a society, or civilization.

urgency.description: Time pressure on consequential decisions or events.

density.description: Amount of spoken dialogue relative to the work's running time.

dependence.description: Importance of understanding dialogue to follow the work.

overlap.description: Use of simultaneous or overlapping speech.

naturalistic_delivery.description: Conversational delivery resembling spontaneous everyday speech.

theatrical_delivery.description: Heightened, rhetorical, or explicitly performative speech.

gothic.description: Ominous, decaying, or romantically macabre visual atmosphere.

noir.description: Shadowed, morally uneasy visual and atmospheric treatment, independently of crime plotting.

retro.description: Deliberately retrospective visual or sonic styling; not merely an older release.

minimalism.description: Reduction of visual, sonic, or formal elements.

stylization.description: Departure from naturalistic presentation through a distinctive audiovisual treatment.

surrealism.description: Dreamlike or illogical relationships in presented images and events.

psychedelia.description: Hallucinatory, distorted, or perceptually altered sensory treatment.

grotesquerie.description: Emphasis on distorted, repulsive, or biologically unsettling forms.

camp.description: Theatrical excess and conspicuous artifice with an invitation to enjoy that excess.

ironic_distance.description: Presentation that invites distance from its apparent surface meaning.

intimacy.description: Presentation fostering closeness to characters' private experience.

spectacle.description: Emphasis on impressive scale, effects, and set pieces.

immersion.description: Strength of the sensory sense of inhabiting the work's world.

lyricism.description: Poetic, associative presentation through image, language, sound or rhythm; not a synonym for slow pacing.

transgression.description: Perceptible aesthetic treatment that deliberately challenges taboos or conventions; do not infer a creator's private intent or equate explicit content alone with transgression.

muted_palette.description: Use of restrained or desaturated colors.

warm_color.description: Prominence of warm hues and lighting.

cool_color.description: Prominence of cool hues and lighting.

low_key_lighting.description: Predominance of dark lighting with selective illumination.

high_key_lighting.description: Predominance of bright, evenly illuminated scenes.

high_contrast.description: Strong contrast between light and dark regions.

long_takes.description: Prominence of extended shots without cuts; method of capture is irrelevant.

handheld_motion.description: Prominence of visibly handheld or unstable camera movement.

production_design_detail.description: Density of expressive detail in constructed environments and props.

cutting_pace.description: Perceived rate of shot changes and editing transitions: 0 means virtually no cuts, not low quality. Distinct from rate of plot events.

martial_arts_choreography.description: Combat organized around recognizable or stylized martial arts movement.

grappling.description: Combat involving holds, clinches, throws, or ground fighting.

blade_combat.description: Combat involving swords, knives, or similar blades.

superpowered_combat.description: Combat involving abilities beyond ordinary human capacities.

large_battles.description: Combat involving many participants or military-scale engagement.

gritty_combat.description: Combat presented as physically punishing, messy, and effortful.

stylized_violence.description: Violence presented through conspicuously aestheticized movement or imagery.

realistic_violence.description: Violence presented with plausible physical consequences and vulnerability.

possession.description: A supernatural entity inhabits or takes control of a person as a horror mechanism. Explicitly excludes psychological dissociation, an alternate personality without supernatural inhabitation, ordinary manipulation or influence, and merely owning or using a magical object.

body_horror.description: Transformation, violation, or instability of the body matters to the horror.

folk_horror.description: Folk belief, ritual, landscape, or insular tradition matters to the horror.

cosmic_horror.description: Human insignificance before incomprehensible forces matters to the horror.

psychological_horror.description: Perception, mental distress, or internal instability drives the horror.

design_prominence.description: Expressive prominence of non-musical sound design; not a quality judgment.

ambient_soundscapes.description: Use of environmental sound to create atmosphere.

silence.description: Expressive use of silence or near silence.

sparse_score.description: Use of little or no non-diegetic score.

audio_startles.description: Abrupt sound events intended to startle.

music_dependence.description: Importance of music to emotional or narrative understanding.

musical_numbers.description: Prominence of song or dance sequences functioning as narrative expression.

conflict_resolution.description: Extent to which central dramatic conflicts receive an outcome; independent of happiness.

interpretive_openness.description: Extent to which the ending permits multiple interpretations.

emotional_closure.description: Extent of emotional completion or release at the ending.

happiness.description: Positive emotional outcome for focal characters at the ending.

tragedy.description: Loss, defeat, or suffering defining the ending.

bittersweetness.description: Intertwined positive and painful outcomes at the ending.

sensory_intensity.description: Strength and density of audiovisual stimulation.
